answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bond-gated identity and cluster detection. Before its attestations count, each agent locks a stake; auditors trace deposits to their source, so a hundred keys drawing on one oasis of funding collapse into one voter. To win ten votes along any ridge of the marketplace an attacker must post ten independent bonds, each slashable when the cluster is exposed. Cost rises linearly with every fake identity while reward per identity stays flat: the crystal of capital a Sybil must risk quickly exceeds anything the raid can earn.
